source_text:
Καὶ ἔλαθεν τὸν ἄρχοντα τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου ἡ παρθενία Μαρίας καὶ ὁ τοκετὸς αὐτῆς, ὁμοίως καὶ ὁ θάνατος τοῦ κυρίου: τρία μυστήρια κραυγῆς, ἅτινα ἐν ἡσυχίᾳ θεοῦ ἐπράχθη.
πῶς οὖν ἐφανερώθη τοῖς αἰῶσιν; ἀστὴρ ἐν οὐρανῷ ἔλαμψεν ὑπὲρ πάντας τοὺς ἀστέρας, καὶ τὸ φῶς αὐτοῦ ἀνεκλάλητον ἦν καὶ ξενισμὸν παρεῖχεν ἡ καινότης αὐτοῦ, τὰ δὲ λοιπὰ πάντα ἄστρα ἅμα ἡλίῳ καὶ σελήνῃ χορὸς ἐγένετο τῷ ἀστέρι, αὐτὸς δὲ ἦν ὑπερβάλλων τὸ φῶς αὐτοῦ ὑπὲρ πάντα: ταραχή τε ἦν, πόθεν ἡ καινότης ἡ ἀνόμοιος αὐτοῖς.
ὅθεν ἐλύετο πᾶσα μαγεία καὶ πᾶς δεσμὸς ἠφανίζετο κακίας: ἄγνοια καθῃρεῖτο, παλαιὰ βασιλεία διεφθείρετο θεοῦ ἀνθρωπίνως φανερουμένου εἰς καινότητα ἀϊδίου ζωῆς: ἀρχὴν δὲ ἐλάμβανεν τὸ παρὰ θεῷ ἀπηρτισμένον. ἔνθεν τὰ πάντα συνεκινεῖτο διὰ τὸ μελετᾶσθαι θανάτου κατάλυσιν.
thought_title: Three mysteries hidden from the ruler of this age
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Ephesians, explaining how the virginity, birth, and death of Jesus were hidden from the devil and then revealed to the ages through the star.
pass_a_gloss: And the virginity of Mary and her giving birth escaped the notice of the ruler of this age, likewise also the death of the Lord: three mysteries of a shout, which were accomplished in the silence of God. How then was it revealed to the ages? A star shone in heaven above all the stars, and its light was unspeakable and its newness caused astonishment, and all the remaining stars together with the sun and moon became a chorus for the star, and it was surpassing its light above all things: and there was disturbance, from where the newness unlike them. From this all magic was being dissolved and every bond of wickedness was being made to disappear: ignorance was being pulled down, the kingdom of the present evil age was being destroyed, God being manifested humanly into newness of eternal life: and what had been completed with God was taking a beginning. From this all things were being set in motion together because of the destruction of death being meditated upon.

choices.why: Fixed glossary rendering for the devil; keeps the cosmic title rather than naming the devil directly.
Literal rendering preserves the paradox of a shout accomplished in silence; 'of a shout' keeps the genitive force.
Literal rendering keeps the divine agency and the contrast with the shout.

choices.english: became a chorus for the star
choices.why: Keeps the image of the heavenly bodies forming a chorus around the star, which is the literal sense.
rejected: formed a choir around the star

choices.why: Literal rendering preserves the contrast with the newness of eternal life that follows.
The perfect participle conveys a finished state with God that now takes a beginning in time.

pass_b_english: The virginity of Mary, her giving birth, and the death of the Lord escaped the notice of the ruler of this age. These are three mysteries proclaimed aloud, yet accomplished in the silence of God.
How then was he revealed to the ages?

A star shone in heaven above all the stars, and its light was unspeakable, and its newness caused astonishment. All the rest of the stars, together with the sun and moon, became a chorus for the star, and it surpassed them all in light. And there was confusion: where did this new thing, so unlike them, come from?

From that moment all sorcery was being dissolved and every bond of wickedness was being made to disappear. Ignorance was being torn down, the ancient kingdom of evil was being destroyed, as God was being revealed in human form for the newness of eternal life. What had been fully prepared with God was now beginning. From then on all things were being stirred together, because the destruction of death was being set in motion.

last_rejected.why: κραυγῆς is genitive; 'of a shout' is odd. The mysteries themselves cry out/proclaim, not 'of a shout'. Better: 'three mysteries that cried out' or 'three mysteries of proclamation'.
last_rejected.ruling: κραυγῆς genitive is standardly 'of a shout/cry'; 'mysteries of a shout' is literal and defensible, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: God was being revealed in human form
last_rejected.why: ἀνθρωπίνως is adverb 'in a human way/manner', not 'in human form'. The revelation was human-like, not that God took human form specifically here.
last_rejected.fix: God being revealed in human fashion
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνθρωπίνως 'in human manner/form' is within normal range; 'in human form' is acceptable, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: What had been completed with God was taking its beginning
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀρχὴν δὲ ἐλάμβανεν τὸ παρὰ θεῷ ἀπηρτισμένον
last_rejected.why: τὸ παρὰ θεῷ ἀπηρτισμένον means 'what had been prepared/perfected by God' or 'with God', but 'taking its beginning' reverses: it was beginning, not taking a beginning that already existed. The sense is 'was beginning' or 'was receiving its beginning'.
last_rejected.fix: What had been prepared by God was beginning
last_rejected.ruling: 'taking its beginning' for ἀρχὴν ἐλάμβανεν is standard idiom 'was beginning'; no reversal, just normal rendering.

last_rejected.quote: all things were being stirred together
last_rejected.why: συνεκινεῖτο is 'were being stirred up/moved together' in sense of turmoil/upheaval, not physically 'stirred together' like mixing. 'All things were being thrown into turmoil/upheaval'.
last_rejected.fix: all things were being thrown into upheaval
last_rejected.ruling: συνεκινεῖτο 'were being moved/stirred together' covers both turmoil and mixing; 'stirred together' is within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: because the destruction of death was being set in motion
last_rejected.why: μελετᾶσθαι is 'being studied/planned/practiced', not 'set in motion'. κατάλυσιν is 'destruction/dissolution'. 'Because the destruction of death was being planned' or 'was coming into being'.
last_rejected.fix: because the destruction of death was being brought to pass
last_rejected.ruling: μελετᾶσθαι can mean 'practiced/prepared/set in motion'; rendering as 'set in motion' is within acceptable range.

polish.changed: Clarified the subject of the first sentence by repeating the three items, kept the opaque phrase 'mysteries of a shout' as the source has it, and broke the passage into three paragraphs where the thought turns from the hidden mysteries to the star's revelation and then to the cosmic effects.

notes.why: 'Mysteries of a shout' is opaque; the word rendered 'shout' is unclear.
notes.fix: Explain or retranslate; the Greek likely means 'proclamation' or 'cry.'

polish.changed: Clarified the speaker as Ignatius throughout, made the three mysteries a clear sentence, replaced 'the kingdom of the present evil age' with 'the ancient kingdom' to avoid adding an unstated gloss, and kept the hymnic star passage as part of Ignatius's own voice.

notes.why: Not same term, but 'old' applied to 'myths' vs. 'kingdom' without reader guidance on what 'old' signifies eschatologically.

notes.quote: A star shone in heaven above all the stars
notes.why: Narrative voice shifts to hymnic/creedal material without marking; reader loses Ignatius's voice.
notes.fix: Format as poetry or inset quotation with note.

polish.changed: Clarified the apparent contradiction in 'three mysteries cried out' by rendering it as 'proclaimed aloud, yet accomplished in the silence of God,' making the contrast explicit while preserving every claim.

notes.quote: three mysteries cried out, accomplished in the silence of God
notes.why: 'Cried out' and 'silence' seem contradictory; reader cannot reconcile.
notes.fix: Note the paradox: mysteries proclaimed by events yet hidden in God's plan.

problems.why: 'Shout' does not fit the context of hidden, silent mysteries; the Greek word likely means 'a cry' in the sense of proclamation, or the translation is too literal.
problems.fix: Consider 'three mysteries proclaimed aloud' or 'three mysteries cried out.'

fixed: Changed 'three mysteries of a shout' to 'three mysteries cried out' to better convey the sense of proclamation while remaining close to the source.

problems.why: Not same term, but 'old' applied to 'myths' vs. 'kingdom' without reader guidance on what 'old' signifies eschatologically.

problems.quote: A star shone in heaven above all the stars
problems.why: Narrative voice shifts to hymnic/creedal material without marking; reader loses Ignatius's voice.
problems.fix: Format as poetry or inset quotation with note.

fixed: The first problem was real: 'old kingdom' did not convey the eschatological sense of the source's 'old kingdom' as the present evil age being destroyed. Changed to 'the kingdom of the present evil age was being destroyed'.
The second problem was real: the hymnic material was not marked. Formatted the passage as inset poetry to signal the shift in voice.

problems.quote: From that moment all magic was being dissolved
problems.why: 'Magic' (mageia) refers to demonic powers, not sleight-of-hand; may seem anachronistic.

edits.old: From that moment all magic was being dissolved
edits.new: From that moment all sorcery was being dissolved

fixed: Changed 'magic' to 'sorcery' to better convey μαγεία as demonic powers rather than sleight-of-hand.

problems.quote: From that moment all sorcery was being dissolved...
problems.why: Unclear whose voice: Ignatius's hymn, Scripture, or prophetic exclamation?

problems.quote: the ancient kingdom was being destroyed
problems.why: 'Ancient kingdom' = Satan's dominion? Or Jewish theocracy? Context suggests former but unclear.
problems.fix: 'the ancient kingdom of evil' or 'of the devil.'

edits.old: the ancient kingdom was being destroyed
edits.new: the ancient kingdom of evil was being destroyed

fixed: The speaker problem is not a mistranslation; the source is Ignatius's own narrative, so no edit is needed.
The source παλαιὰ βασιλεία refers to the old dominion of evil, so 'the ancient kingdom of evil' clarifies without changing the meaning.
